en.headline: Council finds intentional unlawful conduct may have caused Heal Fertility embryo mix-up
en.dek: No embryos were mixed or wrongly implanted; the clinic lacked sufficient protective measures and failed to report the serious event on time, the regulator said.
body: The Council on Human Reproductive Technology said on Friday that its investigation into a mix-up of embryo biopsy specimens at Heal Fertility Limited in Central concluded that intentional unlawful conduct by an individual may have been the main cause. The council confirmed that no embryos were mixed up or wrongly implanted into any person.

The council found that the clinic lacked sufficient protective measures for handling and storing embryos and biopsy specimens, contravening the Code of Practice on Reproductive Technology and Embryo Research. It has ordered the clinic to comply with the ordinance and the code and has set concrete improvement requirements. The clinic’s licence remains under review.

Separately, the Department of Health completed its own investigation under the Private Healthcare Facilities Ordinance. It found the clinic had failed to report the serious untoward event within the required timeframe. The department has taken regulatory action and noted that the clinic has revised its reporting procedures and forms. The council said it would continue to support the police investigation.

zh.headline: 希愈胚胎樣本錯配 管理局指或涉個人蓄意不法行為
zh.dek: 確認無胚胎混淆或錯誤植入；中心防護措施不足且未按時呈報，管理局已要求改善並繼續支援警方調查。
body: 人類生殖科技管理局周五表示，已完成對中環希愈生殖醫學中心胚胎活檢組織樣本錯配事件的調查。管理局接納報告指，事件主要成因或涉及個人蓄意不法行為，並確認事件中並無任何胚胎被混淆或錯誤植入人體。
管理局認為，中心未有對胚胎及活檢組織樣本的處理與儲存採取足夠防護措施，違反《生殖科技及胚胎研究實務守則》相關規定。局方已嚴正指示中心恪守條例及守則，並訂立具體改善要求，中心牌照仍在審視中。
衞生署亦完成根據《私營醫療機構條例》的調查，認為中心未在規定時限內呈報重要風險事件。署方已採取規管行動，並知悉中心已修訂呈報程序及表格。管理局表示會繼續為警方調查提供專業支援。
